name: Palmitoylethanolamide (PEA)
short: Trial data up to 49 days argue against serious reactions at 1 in 200 or more; generally well tolerated, but long-term data and side-effect reporting are limited.
text: A review of 16 clinical trials, 6 case reports or pilot studies and a meta-analysis found that, for treatment up to 49 days, the data argue against serious adverse drug reactions at an incidence of 1 in 200 or greater, but for treatment longer than 60 days too few patients have been studied to rule out reactions at frequencies below 1 in 100. A meta-analysis of pain trials found PEA generally well tolerated, although side-effect assessment in the underlying studies was often poor, and a meta-analysis in diabetic neuropathic pain reported only mild, self-limited adverse events. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.

quotes: Sixteen clinical trials, six case reports/pilot studies and a meta-analysis of PEA as an analgesic have been published in the literature.
For treatment times up to 49 days, the current clinical data argue against serious adverse drug reactions (ADRs) at an incidence of 1/200 or greater.
For treatment lasting more than 60 days, the number of patients is insufficient to rule out a frequency of ADRs of less than 1/100.
